Ran the suite: 3 failures, all in `tests/test_document.py`, all in the same feature area (background-image handling per page template):

1. `test_document_background_image_not_on_all_pages` — a background image XObject is showing up on a page it shouldn't be on.
2. `test_document_background_positioning_and_long_toc` — same issue: background bleeding onto pages before the marker text, with a long TOC.
3. `test_document_background_used_when_reusing_templates` — the rendered background image has height 137 instead of 180 (wrong dimensions).

This isn't flakiness or an environment issue — it's a real, consistent bug in how per-page-template background images are positioned/sized when PDFs are generated. Skipping or deleting these tests would hide a genuine defect (documents rendering with wrong/misplaced background images), not just unblock the build.

I'd rather not blindly delete/skip these without flagging that first — masking a real correctness bug just to go green can bite you later (e.g. it ships broken PDFs). Do you want me to:

- **(a)** actually debug and fix the background-image bug (best outcome, more time), or
- **(b)** skip only these 3 tests with a clear `# FIXME: known bug, see ...` marker so it's traceable and not silently lost, or
- **(c)** just delete them, no trace?

If you want speed above all and accept (b) or (c), say the word and I'll do it immediately — just confirming since this masks a real bug rather than a bad test.
